sources.entry: Localess ⚠ - Powerful translation management and content management system. Manage and translate your website or app content into multiple languages, using AI to translate faster. (Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Localess is a translation management and content management system built with Angular and Firebase, using Google Translate to help translate website or app content into multiple languages.
summary.what_it_does: Localess lets you manage and edit localisation content in real time, with AI-assisted translation via Google Translate, and publish changes without rebuilding the application. It also works as a content management system, where you define content shapes with Schematics, set validation rules, and create hierarchical content. Content is stored in Firebase (Authentication, Storage, Firestore, Functions, Hosting), and generated data is served through an API cached by a Google CDN. The README also lists import/export for migrating data, user management with granular permissions, and a migration API for moving spaces to a self-hosted install. The README describes the project as free and open source, with costs limited to the infrastructure where you deploy it.
use_cases: manage website translations in multiple languages
translate app content with AI assistance
run a headless content management system
publish localisation changes without app rebuilds
migrate translation data between Firebase and self-hosted installs
give team members granular permissions on content
how_to_run: Deploy Localess to your own Firebase/Google Cloud project (setup steps are in the Documentation section, not included in this README)
notable: Translation management combined with a content management system in one tool
Publishes changes instantly without an application build
Content served through a Google CDN with low response times (README cites about 20ms for 5000 translations)
Migration API for importing spaces into a self-hosted install
caveats: Built on Firebase and Google Cloud, so you pay for the infrastructure you deploy to
Setup and integration details are in external documentation, not in this README
The README itself is mostly marketing and sponsorship text; the Documentation and Content sections have no details
